findings.title: Bare `include_website_name` is never called, so the filter does not apply
findings.detail: The serializer's include hook is named `include_website_name?` with a question mark. Without it, `website_name` is always serialized, and `website` is hidden for restricted TL0 users (via untrusted_attributes) but `website_name` leaks. The spec's untrusted-attribute list also omits website_name.

findings.title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string and the subdomain match is wrong
findings.detail: `ends_with?("-." << website_host)` is correct only by accident of the literal being a fresh string; the check also treats any host that is a suffix of the forum host as the 'parent' (e.g. website 'com' or unrelated). The same-length branch compares only the tail labels so 'www.example.com' vs 'forum.example.com' matches but 'a.co.uk' vs 'forum.example.com' mismatches. Logic is brittle for multi-label TLDs.

findings.title: Unguarded `.host` / `.path` on non-HTTP URIs and rescue only on first parse
findings.detail: `URI(...)` is re-parsed later without the rescue, and for URIs such as `mailto:` the host is nil (handled), but for generic URIs `path` may be nil for opaque URIs causing `website_host + nil` TypeError. Also `website` without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com') returns host nil so no name is shown, a regression from the former client-side split behavior.

findings.title: Full path appended produces trailing slash/long names for root URLs
findings.detail: When hosts match, the path is appended unconditionally, so a website 'http://example.com/' displays as 'example.com/' with a trailing slash.

findings.title: Tests miss the same-length sibling-subdomain branch and the nil/invalid case
findings.detail: The new specs cover only three of the branches; the www vs forum branch, invalid URL, and TL0 hiding of website_name are untested.

findings.title: Mutating string with << inside ends_with? check
findings.detail: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal in place, which breaks when frozen string literals are enabled. The suffix check also uses the raw host and drops any port or path context, so the results can be unreliable.

findings.title: website_name bypasses untrusted-attribute restriction
findings.detail: `website` is hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors, but `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. The derived host and path are still exposed, and the profile template will render a globe icon and name.

findings.title: Same-level subdomain heuristic is wrong
findings.detail: The branch for equal label counts compares everything after the first label, which wrongly treats unrelated hosts as the same site. For example `foo.example.co.uk` vs `forum.example.co.uk` behaves differently from what the comment implies. It also ignores the case where the website is `a.com` and the forum is `b.a.com` at deeper levels.

findings.title: Unguarded path/hostname handling can raise or produce odd output
findings.detail: Only the first URI parse is protected by rescue. The later `URI(website.to_s).path` calls are unprotected, and `Discourse.current_hostname` is used before the nil check. A website without a path, or one with a trailing slash, yields names like `example.com/`.

findings.title: include_website_name lacks trailing ?
findings.detail: ActiveModel serializers look for `include_website_name?`. Without the question mark the method is never called, so the attribute is always included, possibly as nil.

findings.title: Tests miss the equal-label-count branch and edge cases
findings.detail: The specs cover only three hosts. The `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch, an empty path, a nil/invalid website, and the anonymous TL0 hiding of `website_name` are never tested.

findings.title: Parent-domain check uses mutating `<<` on a literal
findings.detail: `"." << website_host` builds the string correctly, but the logic only covers the case where the website is a parent of the forum host. It does not treat `forum.example.com` or a sibling like `www.example.com` consistently, and the branch order means the second branch (same label count) swallows the case without a parent comparison. Behaviour differs from the stated comments.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain comparison is wrong for multi-part TLDs and unrelated domains
findings.detail: Comparing everything after the first label treats `foo.co.uk` and `bar.co.uk` style hosts (and any same-depth hosts with identical suffix, e.g. `a.github.io` vs `b.github.io`) as the same site, so the full path is shown for unrelated sites.

findings.title: Website parse failure/unsupported URIs not handled; path may be nil or fully qualified wrongly
findings.detail: `rescue nil` modifier silently swallows all errors. `URI(...)` for relative or schemeless values like `example.com` gives a nil host and no website_name is shown, a regression from the old split-based display. Mailto/other schemes behave inconsistently.

findings.title: include_website_name defined without trailing '?' and bypasses untrusted restriction
findings.detail: ActiveModel::Serializer looks up `include_website_name?`. The method `include_website_name` is never called, so the attribute is always included (nil when no website). Also, website_name is not added to untrusted_attributes, so it leaks the website host of TL0 users to anonymous viewers, which the website attribute hides.

findings.title: Same-host branch appends path that may be empty or nil-dependent; trailing slash and query ignored
findings.detail: When the host matches, the displayed name is host plus path only, dropping query/fragment; with an empty path it equals the host. Also `discourse_host.split` is evaluated before nil safety is guaranteed for Discourse.current_hostname.

findings.title: Tests miss sibling-subdomain branch and edge cases
findings.detail: The specs cover only three cases; the middle branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com), invalid URIs, and anonymous TL0 hiding of website_name are untested.

findings.title: Nil TopicUser crashes unsubscribe for users without a topic_users row
findings.detail: TopicUser.find_by can return nil when the user never visited or has no record for the topic, so calling notification_level on it raises NoMethodError and a 500. Nothing guards against nil.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe performed on GET request
findings.detail: A GET endpoint modifies the user's notification level. Any page, image tag or link prefetcher can trigger it for a logged-in user without CSRF protection, and it skips check_xhr.

findings.title: Repeated visits/refreshes escalate to mute; not idempotent
findings.detail: Each visit lowers the level: watching/tracking becomes regular, and a second load (refresh, email prefetch) becomes muted. Users who only meant to stop notifications end up muting the topic.

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses topic access checks and ignores notification side effects
findings.detail: The topic user's level is saved directly with save! instead of TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id, notifications_changed_at and the MessageBus update are not set. The client may show a stale state.

findings.title: Slug redirect occurs before JSON format handling and uses 301 for a state-changing path
findings.detail: The permanent 301 redirect for a missing slug is cached by browsers. Since the action is not idempotent, and redirect happens via unsubscribe_url without the .json suffix, JSON requests are redirected to an HTML URL.

findings.title: Triple-stash renders title-derived HTML unescaped
findings.detail: The text is rendered unescaped, relying on fancyTitle being sanitized by the server. Any title content not escaped will lead to XSS.

findings.title: Misspelled property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
findings.detail: The name is misspelled in both the controller and template; it works only because they match, and it is error-prone for later use.

findings.title: Unsubscribe link missing when no unsubscribe_url given
findings.detail: The new unsubscribe_link locale string requires %{unsubscribe_url}. Emails built with add_unsubscribe_link but without unsubscribe_url (e.g. other mailers) will fail the I18n interpolation or render a broken link.

findings.title: Nil TopicUser dereference crashes unsubscribe
findings.detail: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the user has no topic_users row (e.g. never visited the topic), so `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError and results in a 500.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed via GET
findings.detail: The unsubscribe action mutates the user's notification level on a plain GET request. Any link, image, or email-client prefetcher can trigger it, and there is no confirmation or CSRF protection.

findings.title: Repeated visits escalate from regular to muted
findings.detail: Notification level is lowered to regular if it was above regular, otherwise it is set to muted. A second hit on the link, such as a refresh, a prefetch, or reloading the page, silently mutes the topic instead of being idempotent.

findings.title: Unsubscribe redirect target is broken or loops
findings.detail: The redirect is sent when params[:slug] is blank, but it uses the unsubscribe_url built from `url`. Slug mismatch for JSON requests redirects to an HTML URL. The redirect also happens before access checks, since TopicView.new can fail for inaccessible topics. The state change runs only after the redirect check, so the redirect itself is not always the issue, but non-JSON requests with a wrong slug lose the unsubscribe intent only when the client does not follow the redirect.

findings.title: Triple-stache rendering of interpolated title
findings.detail: stopNotificiationsText embeds the topic's fancyTitle into an HTML string that is rendered unescaped. If fancyTitle is not fully sanitized this allows script injection, and any non-escaped title text would break the markup.

findings.title: Explicit render :show added to shared response path
findings.detail: perform_show_response is shared by show and unsubscribe, so `render :show` is now forced for both. This is needed for unsubscribe because the template would otherwise be looked up as 'unsubscribe', but it silently changes the shared path.

findings.title: afterModel mutation may hit undefined details
findings.detail: topic.set('details.notificationReasonText', null) assumes topic.details exists after updateFromJson. The mutation also persists on the shared topic record and can hide the reason text elsewhere.

findings.title: Misspelled property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
findings.detail: The computed property name is misspelled, so the name is inconsistent with its i18n key stop_notifications. It is consistently used in the template, so this is only a maintainability risk.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when user has no TopicUser record
findings.detail: TopicUser.find_by returns nil if the user never visited or tracked the topic, for example a mailing-list recipient. The following `tu.notification_level` call then raises NoMethodError and returns a 500.

findings.title: State-changing action performed on a GET request
findings.detail: The unsubscribe action modifies notification_level and saves on a plain GET route, with check_xhr skipped. Any page, image tag or link prefetch can trigger mute/unwatch for a logged-in user without CSRF protection.

findings.title: Repeated visit escalates from regular to muted
findings.detail: A level above regular is lowered to regular, and a level of regular or lower is set to muted. Reloading the page, or a second click on the email link, mutes the topic, which differs from the page text that says notifications will stop.

findings.title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change
findings.detail: Setting notification_level via tu.save! skips TopicUser.change, so notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id are not updated and the MessageBus notification_level_change message is not published. Clients showing the notification button may be stale.

findings.title: Redirect on slug mismatch happens before topic access check
findings.detail: Redirecting 301 on slug mismatch means a permanent redirect is cached for a state-changing URL. The TopicView is created with params[:topic_id] before any guard handling, and the redirect path itself does not perform the unsubscribe.

findings.title: Triple-stash renders unescaped topic title
findings.detail: {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} outputs raw HTML built from the topic's fancyTitle. Any markup in fancyTitle is injected unescaped.

findings.title: Misspelled property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
findings.detail: The name is misspelled in the controller and in the template. It still works, but it is easy to mistype and break consistency.

findings.title: Explicit `render :show` added to shared perform_show_response
findings.detail: The unsubscribe action now renders the show template via perform_show_response, so a successful visit calls the show template, unlike the other callers, which rely on implicit rendering. This changes shared behavior for every caller.

findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition overrides the 4-arg version
findings.detail: Two `self.downsize` methods are defined; the later 3-arg (from, to, dimensions, opts) silently replaces the earlier (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts). Existing callers passing width and height now bind height to `dimensions`/`opts` and break (e.g. a numeric height passed as opts, producing wrong dimensions or errors).
findings.evidence: def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})

findings.title: Downsize loop does not update tempfile size and may corrupt the file
findings.detail: `tempfile.size` on a Tempfile can be stale because it is buffered by the Ruby object; the loop may not see the reduced size. Converting in-place, `convert` writes to the same path it reads and `-resize 80%` is applied repeatedly. If conversion fails, nothing is detected and the loop keeps retrying.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores site settings for non-image attachments
findings.detail: Client-side check now uses a fixed 10MB for all types, including attachments, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb. Attachments over the configured limit now pass client validation and only fail on the server, and the admin setting no longer controls the client check.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded, ignoring configured size
findings.detail: The download limit is now a hardcoded 10MB regardless of site settings, so attachment size limits are bypassed on download and the server may fetch more than intended.

findings.title: 413 error message shows hardcoded size
findings.detail: The 413 handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit that may not match the actual web-server or site limit, giving a misleading message.

findings.title: Possible nil filename in is_image? check
findings.detail: In the API URL branch, `filename` is derived from the URL path and may be empty. Also `content_type` is unset in that branch. `FileHelper.is_image?` is called without guarding for these cases.

findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition overrides the 4-arg version
findings.detail: The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`. Existing callers that pass width and height separately now have their height treated as `dimensions` and their opts lost or misrouted, so they break or produce wrong dimensions.

findings.title: Downsize loop passes a hash into the opts slot but may be misrouted and can corrupt the tempfile
findings.detail: With the duplicate `downsize` definition, the call with `"80%"` and an options hash only works because the 3-arg version wins. The loop also overwrites the file in place using `tempfile.path`, and `tempfile.size` on the Tempfile object may stay stale because of buffering. In that case the loop re-runs all 5 attempts, or never sees the reduced size. ImageMagick failures are also ignored, so a failed conversion is retried five times.

findings.title: Animated GIF path uses gifsicle --resize-fit with a percentage
findings.detail: For animated GIFs, `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to gifsicle `--resize-fit "80%"`. That option expects WxH and does not accept a percentage, so the command fails and the oversized GIF is never reduced.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download limit ignores configured size settings
findings.detail: The URL download limit is fixed at 10 MB instead of using the site setting. Non-image files (type attachment) are no longer limited by `max_attachment_size_kb`, and the client-side check now also ignores it.

findings.title: Client-side size check ignores per-type setting and attachment limits
findings.detail: The `max_<type>_size_kb` setting is replaced by a constant 10 MB for both images and attachments. Attachments can therefore exceed the configured limit on the client, and the error message reports 10 MB rather than the configured limit.

findings.title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded size
findings.detail: A 413 comes from the web server, whose limit is not tied to this constant. The message therefore states a made-up limit rather than the real one.

findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition overrides the 4-arg version
findings.detail: The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`. Existing callers passing width and height now have the height treated as `dimensions` and the opts as a hash, which breaks them or produces wrong ImageMagick arguments.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and only reduces by 80% of dimensions
findings.detail: The return value of `downsize` is never checked, so a failed conversion still repeats the loop. Also `tempfile.size` may be cached or stale, and an animated GIF uses gifsicle with `--resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid dimension. Large files can end up uploaded despite being over the limit, with no error reported.

findings.title: Resize guard breaks for API URL path and nil filename
findings.detail: `filename` is derived from the URL path and may lack an image extension, in which case the resize is skipped. `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` on a nil filename could also raise. Non-image attachments are no longer size-limited by the server setting anyway.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB limit replaces per-type site settings
findings.detail: The client no longer honors `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb`, so attachments that exceed the attachment limit pass client validation and the error message reports 10MB instead of the real limit. The magic number is also duplicated across files.

findings.title: API download limit hardcoded, ignoring site setting
findings.detail: Remote downloads now allow 10MB regardless of `max_image_size_kb`, and this applies to non-image files as well. Downloaded non-images are not reduced afterwards, so the configured limit can be bypassed unless Upload.create_for re-checks it.

findings.title: Validation has a side effect and runs on every valid? call
findings.detail: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and saves inside a validator. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, so each signup attempt is counted twice. Any other valid? call also inflates the stats.

findings.title: Email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
findings.detail: The exact-match lookup means a blocked address can be bypassed by changing case, for example Bad@x.com versus bad@x.com. The email is not downcased before the query or before storing.

findings.title: Non-atomic counter increment
findings.detail: match_count is read, incremented in Ruby and saved, so concurrent signups lose updates. An atomic increment such as update_all or increment_counter avoids this. The save result is also ignored.

findings.title: Whitelist/blacklist check crashes on nil or non-string value
findings.detail: The validator is attached with `if: :email_changed?` but no allow_nil. If the email is nil, the regexp match returns nil and the whitelist branch adds an error, so the presence error is duplicated. The blocked-email lookup also runs with a nil value.

findings.title: Shared array instance in controller prototype
findings.detail: Em.A([]) in the extend() hash is shared by all instances of the controller. Rejected emails persist across instances and are never cleared. An init-time array would be safer.

findings.title: Any email error marks the email as invalid with a generic message
findings.detail: All email errors, including a duplicate email, add the email to rejectedEmails. The field then shows the generic 'invalid' reason, which is misleading. The server error message is not used.

findings.title: Validator spec passes attributes as a symbol and mocks the logic under test
findings.detail: The spec builds the validator with `attributes: :email`, and the whitelist/blacklist paths are not covered. The new error-skipping branch (`errors[attribute].blank?`) is not tested either.

findings.title: Validation has side effects and case-sensitive matching
findings.detail: should_block? writes to the DB (match_count/last_match_at) every time it is called from a validator; user.valid? is called multiple times in the create flow (valid? then save), so counts are double-incremented, and updates are non-atomic (lost updates under concurrency). Also the lookup is an exact-case match, so differently-cased emails bypass the block.

findings.title: Blocked email check skipped when other email errors exist
findings.detail: The block check is gated on record.errors[attribute].blank?, which also includes errors from earlier validators (e.g. presence/uniqueness on email). Behaviour depends on validator order and the blocked-email lookup/stat update is skipped; also the validator is invoked with a nil value if email is nil in some paths, causing `value =~ regexp` on nil and a DB query with nil.

findings.title: Shared rejectedEmails array on the prototype
findings.detail: Em.A([]) in the extend() hash is created once and shared by all instances of the controller; rejected emails persist across modal sessions and instances. It should be initialized in init.

findings.title: Rejected email list affects all email errors and uses stale values
findings.detail: Any email error (including uniqueness or invalid format) pushes the email into the rejected list, and the rejected state shows a generic 'invalid' reason rather than the server error. Also matching is case-sensitive versus server-side handling.

findings.title: Echoing user attributes via attributes.slice
findings.detail: Using user.attributes.slice with string keys relies on Hash#slice and returns raw submitted values; combined with errors.to_hash this adds response fields without need for username/name. Minor but unnecessary exposure of input and potential reliance on ActiveSupport slice behavior.

findings.title: Validator spec does not cover whitelist/blacklist behavior moved into validator
findings.detail: The whitelist/blacklist logic was moved to EmailValidator but the spec only tests the blocked-email branch with a stubbed model, so the moved domain restriction branches are untested. The validator is also constructed with attributes: :email (not an array).

findings.title: Validation has write side effects, and the counter update can lose increments
findings.detail: should_block? is called from a validator, so every validation (including user.valid? followed by user.save in UsersController#create) increments match_count and updates last_match_at. One signup attempt therefore counts twice or more. The read-modify-write increment is also not atomic, so concurrent attempts can lose updates.

findings.title: Email lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized
findings.detail: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is an exact match and the model never downcases or strips the stored email. A blocked address can be bypassed by changing case (Bad@Spam.com vs bad@spam.com).

findings.title: should_block? returns nil instead of a boolean
findings.detail: When no record exists, `record && ...` evaluates to nil rather than false. Callers that expect a strict boolean can misbehave, and the spec's `be_false` only passes because nil is falsy under this RSpec version.

findings.title: Blocked-email check skipped when other email errors exist
findings.detail: The check runs only when record.errors[attribute] is blank. That includes errors added by earlier validators such as presence or uniqueness. In those cases blocked-email matches are not counted and no blocked error is reported.

findings.title: Regex match on a possibly nil value
findings.detail: validate_each can receive a nil email. `nil =~ regexp` happens to return nil without raising, so a whitelist check treats a missing email as not allowed and adds a duplicate 'not allowed' error alongside the presence error. The domain list is also interpolated into a regex unescaped except for dots.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is shared across controller instances
findings.detail: Em.A([]) in the class body creates one array on the prototype that is shared by all instances. Rejected emails persist across modal uses and are never reset.

findings.title: Invalid '@each' dependent key
findings.detail: 'rejectedEmails.@each' has no property after @each. Ember expects 'rejectedEmails.[]' or 'rejectedEmails.@each.prop', so the validation may not recompute when an email is pushed.

findings.title: Any server-side email error marks the email as rejected
findings.detail: Any error on the email field (for example, a transient not_allowed or a taken email) adds the email to rejectedEmails. The validation then shows 'invalid' instead of the real server reason.

findings.title: Validator spec passes a symbol where an array is expected and only covers stubbed paths
findings.detail: The validator is built with `attributes: :email` instead of an array. The spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and never exercises the whitelist/blacklist domain branches that moved into this class.

findings.title: Light-theme colour changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.detail: The original colour was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The light branch is now 70%, so link text becomes much lighter and less readable in the default theme, and the dark branch is not its counterpart either.

findings.title: Mismatched lightness values in dark-light-choose for custom-message-length
findings.detail: The original light value was 70%. The new light branch uses 30% while the dark branch uses 70%, so the pair is not mirrored. Light-theme text becomes much darker, which is an unintended visual change.

findings.title: Light-theme colour of .name altered from 30% to 50%
findings.detail: The original colour was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses 50%/50%, which lightens the name in the light theme. This looks like a copy-paste of the neighbouring .title rule.

findings.title: Light-theme colour of .name altered from 30% to 50%
findings.detail: The original colour was 30% lightness. The replacement uses 50%/50%, which lightens the name in the light theme. This looks like a copy-paste of the neighbouring .title rule.

findings.title: Light-theme colour of h3 changed from 20% to 50%
findings.detail: The original h3 colour was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), a strong heading colour. The replacement uses 50%/50%, which weakens the heading contrast in the light theme. The desktop equivalent correctly uses 20%/80%.

findings.title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.detail: The original value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The light branch now uses 70%, so usernames in this block become much paler in the normal theme, a regression unrelated to dark-mode support. The dark value (secondary 30%) is also not the mirror of the light one.

findings.title: Name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness in light theme
findings.detail: The original was $primary at 30% lightness. The change alters the light-theme appearance, making the name as light as the title beneath it, and loses the visual hierarchy.

findings.title: Mobile name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.detail: Same as the desktop variant. The original light value was $primary at 30%, and the change alters the light-theme appearance and removes the name/title distinction.

findings.title: Light value changed from 70% to 30% and dark value mismatched
findings.detail: The original light color was $primary at 70% lightness. It is now 30% (much darker), so the light theme changes and the hint text becomes more prominent. Desktop modal.scss uses 70%/30% for the same rule.

findings.title: Mobile suggested-topic h3 color changed from 20% to 50%
findings.detail: The original light color was $primary at 20% lightness. The new 50%/50% values lighten the heading in the light theme, a regression. They also differ from the desktop equivalent (20%/80%).

findings.title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.detail: The original light value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light branch uses 70%, which makes the author link in the post-reply preview noticeably lighter in the default theme, and it is inconsistent with the 70/30 pairing of the dark value.

findings.title: Light-theme .name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.detail: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The change alters the light-theme appearance of the user name in the card (lighter than before) instead of only adding a dark variant.

findings.title: Mobile .name color light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.detail: The original light color was primary 30%. The new light branch is primary 50%, a regression in the light theme's contrast; it also no longer matches the 30/70 pairing used for the same element in common/user.scss.

findings.title: Mobile h3 color light value changed from 20% to 50%
findings.detail: The original light color was primary 20%. The new light branch is primary 50%, making the heading much lighter in the default theme. The dark value is also not the complement of the original (20/80).

findings.title: Mobile .custom-message-length light value changed from 70% to 30%
findings.detail: The original light color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new light branch is 30%, which changes the light-theme appearance and is inconsistent with the desktop counterpart (70/30).

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive against lowercased column
findings.detail: The query compares lower(host) to the raw URI host without downcasing it. A referer with uppercase letters (e.g. Example.COM) fails to match, and URI#host is not normalized to lowercase.

findings.title: Category fabricators deleted and replaced with embeddable_host fabricator
findings.detail: category_fabricator.rb now contains only the embeddable_host fabricator, while the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, etc.) were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The contents appear swapped between files. Fabricator loading may work by accident, but the filenames contradict their contents and make the specs confusing.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host and mutates in place
findings.detail: self.host.sub! raises NoMethodError when host is nil, so a missing host param becomes a 500 instead of a validation error. sub! also mutates the string in place and may hit frozen strings.

findings.title: Missing record leads to nil dereference in update/destroy
findings.detail: When the id does not exist, `host` is nil, so host.destroy (and save_host) raises NoMethodError and returns 500 rather than a 404. Use find or raise a not-found error.

findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed_category row exists and interpolates raw values in SQL
findings.detail: `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError on nil when no embed_category setting exists (the common default), aborting the migration. In addition, hosts are interpolated into SQL without escaping or trimming, and legacy values with http:// or paths bypass model normalization.

findings.title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil/record
findings.detail: It returns false on invalid input but a record or nil otherwise; the inconsistent return type is passed to `eh.try(:category_id)` in TopicEmbed. Also, `category: eh.try(:category_id)` passes nil when no host record is found, silently losing the category.

findings.title: Host model category set after save may be wrong; categoryId not reset for new hosts
findings.detail: After save, host.category is set from categoryId, but for a new record the form's categoryId is null so no category is displayed, while the server substitutes uncategorized. Also the server-rendered category_id is not used to update the record.

findings.title: Array hydration yields undefined entries and `|| []` is dead code
findings.detail: The map result is always an array, so `|| []` never applies, and ids not found in the root yield undefined entries in the array. Also, obj[k] being null/undefined for an *_ids key would throw.

findings.title: type.replace only replaces first underscore
findings.detail: String.replace with a string pattern only replaces the first occurrence, so types with multiple underscores will not normalize.

findings.title: saveChanges action is unused and update is a no-op
findings.detail: saveChanges calls update with an empty object, and the server update just re-renders the embedding; it does nothing and is never wired in the template.

findings.title: Controller spec only checks inheritance
findings.detail: The spec asserts only the class hierarchy, so it covers none of the create, update, or destroy behavior or the error paths.

findings.title: Category fabricators deleted and replaced with embeddable_host fabricator
findings.detail: category_fabricator.rb now defines only :embeddable_host, and the original category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. :embeddable_host is now defined in a file named for categories, and :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category sit in a file named for embeddable hosts. The fabricators still load, but the files are swapped and misnamed, which is confusing and fragile.

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive against lowercased column
findings.detail: The query compares lower(host) with the URI host without lowercasing it. URI#host preserves case, so a referer like http://EvilTrout.com will not match. The same function is also used with the already-normalized embed URL in TopicEmbed.import.

findings.title: before_validation mutates host in place and crashes on nil
findings.detail: host.sub! raises NoMethodError when host is nil, for example when params[:embeddable_host][:host] is missing. The in-place mutation also modifies the original string and fails on frozen strings.

findings.title: Missing record leads to nil dereference (500)
findings.detail: update and destroy fetch with .where(...).first and use the result without checking for nil. A non-existent id produces NoMethodError and a 500 rather than a 404.

findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed_category setting exists and inserts unescaped values
findings.detail: execute(...)[0]['id'] raises NoMethodError (nil[]) when the embed_category setting is absent, which is the common case. The host value from site_settings is also interpolated into SQL unescaped and unstripped, so a host containing a quote or a carriage return breaks the insert or yields bad data. Existing http:// prefixes are also copied unnormalized.

findings.title: Category passed as an id where PostCreator expects a category name/object
findings.detail: PostCreator's :category option is resolved as a category name/slug, but an integer category_id is passed. The previous code passed the category name from the setting. Topics will not land in the configured category, and the nil fallback silently uses the default.

findings.title: Plural hydration does not handle missing or non-array values; `|| []` is dead code
findings.detail: obj[k].map always returns an array so the fallback never applies. Ids not found in root yield undefined entries, and the ids key is deleted unconditionally.

findings.title: saveChanges calls update on a model with no matching template action
findings.detail: saveChanges calls update({}) on the embedding, which does nothing useful because the server update just re-renders. The action is dead and misleading.

findings.title: Controller specs only assert class inheritance
findings.detail: The specs check only that the controller subclasses AdminController. They do not exercise create, update or destroy, so none of the new logic is covered.

findings.title: Category fabricators deleted and replaced by embeddable_host fabricator
findings.detail: The category, diff_category, happy_category and private_category fabricators were removed from category_fabricator.rb. The file now only defines :embeddable_host, so the existing specs that Fabricate(:category) will fail. The fabricator contents appear to have been swapped between the two files.

findings.title: embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators
findings.detail: The file holds category fabricators, not :embeddable_host. The :embeddable_host fabricator lives in category_fabricator.rb, so the file contents are swapped and load-order dependent. Duplicate definitions of :category could raise DuplicateFabricatorError.

findings.title: Unescaped setting values interpolated into INSERT SQL
findings.detail: Host values from the site setting are interpolated directly into raw SQL. A value containing a quote breaks the migration or allows injection, and trailing whitespace or CR characters are not stripped.
findings.evidence: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"

findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent
findings.detail: `execute(...)[0]['id']` indexes the first row of a result that is empty when no embed_category setting exists (the common case). `[0]` is nil, so nil['id'] raises NoMethodError and the migration fails. The uncategorized_category_id lookup has the same problem.

findings.title: Host lookup is not normalized to lowercase
findings.detail: The query compares lower(host) to the referer host without downcasing it, and the stored host is not downcased on save. Mixed-case hosts and referers will not match. Also, a record stored with a port will never equal uri.host.

findings.title: before_validation mutates host in place and crashes on nil
findings.detail: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil (for example when the param is missing). The in-place mutation also modifies frozen or shared strings and bypasses dirty tracking.

findings.title: Missing record leads to nil dereference
findings.detail: `where(...).first` returns nil for an unknown id, so `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 404.

findings.title: Category passed as id to PostCreator category option
findings.detail: PostCreator's `category` option expects a category name or slug, but a category_id integer is passed. The topic will not land in the configured category (the fix would be to use `category_id`). It is also nil when no host record matches.

findings.title: saveChanges calls update on embedding without a matching template action
findings.detail: `saveChanges` calls `update({})` on a model that is not saved to a real id, and no template references the action. This is dead code that would send a meaningless PUT.

findings.title: Plural id hydration may include undefined entries and misparses keys
findings.detail: `_lookupSubType` can return undefined for ids missing from the root, producing undefined entries in the array. `hydrated || []` is always truthy for an array, so the fallback is pointless. The `_ids` regex also now hijacks any key ending in `_ids`.

findings.title: replace('_','-') only replaces the first underscore
findings.detail: String.replace with a string pattern only replaces the first occurrence, so types with several underscores are not normalized to match ADMIN_MODELS.

findings.title: Flex container makes the existing float rules on children inert
findings.detail: `.small-action` becomes a flex container, but the `button { float: right; }` and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` rules remain. Floats are ignored on flex items, so the right-aligned button (undo/edit action) now sits directly after the description instead of at the right edge.

findings.title: Small-action description padding changed to percentage, losing the avatar offset
findings.detail: The 4em left padding and vertical padding are replaced by `0 1.5%`. The spacing now varies with container width and the vertical spacing is gone. Combined with `.custom-message p { margin: 0 }`, multi-paragraph custom messages lose paragraph spacing.

findings.title: Nonexistent `-ms-align-items` property emitted by the align-items mixin
findings.detail: `-ms-align-items` is not a real CSS property, so it is dead output in every include. The line above it also has trailing whitespace.

findings.title: Global `order` on .extra-info-wrapper has no scoping to the flex header
findings.detail: `order: 2` is applied to every `.extra-info-wrapper` anywhere, not just inside the header's flex `.contents`. The header's `.title` sibling has no explicit order, so the layout relies on implicit order 0 and on the DOM structure.

findings.title: Invalid/incorrect legacy prefixed align-items declarations
findings.detail: The old 2009 `-webkit-box-align` only accepts start/end/center/baseline/stretch, so `flex-start`/`flex-end` passed to the mixin yield invalid values. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property. The mixin emits wrong or dead declarations for common values.

findings.title: Nonexistent `display: -moz-box` is emitted without matching `-moz-inline-box` handling
findings.detail: The flexbox mixin and the inline-flex mixin use mismatched legacy values; `-moz-inline-box` and `-webkit-inline-box` are legacy values requiring matching old `box-align` properties. The `-moz-box-align` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` pairing is missing for align-items, so Firefox 2009 syntax is inconsistently supported.

findings.title: Flex container with floated children and removed `.title` float
findings.detail: `.contents` becomes a flex container and the `.title` float is removed. `.panel` relies on `margin-left:auto` and `order(3)`, but the logo/title element has no explicit order. Other elements such as `.valign-helper` (inline-block, height:100%) now become flex items with odd sizing. This may alter header layout.

findings.title: Flex container combined with floats and `clear: both` on .small-action
findings.detail: `.small-action` becomes a flex container while children still use `float`, which is ignored for flex items. The `.small-action-desc .avatar` float and `button` float:right no longer work. The button also no longer is pushed right.

findings.title: `order` applied to .extra-info-wrapper without flex parent guarantee
findings.detail: `.extra-info-wrapper` is globally styled with `order: 2`, but it only has effect when its parent is a flex container. Other places it appears (outside `.d-header .contents`) get no effect. The removal of the `&.bullet` margin-top affects `#topic-title` separately.

findings.title: Floated action button ignored once .small-action becomes a flex container
findings.detail: `.small-action` is now a flex container, but the existing `button { float: right; }` rule and the `.topic-avatar` float are unchanged. Floats have no effect on flex items, so the right-aligned button will now sit next to the description instead of at the right edge (e.g. `margin-left: auto` would be needed).

findings.title: align-items mixin emits a nonexistent property and passes modern values to legacy properties
findings.detail: `-ms-align-items` is not a real vendor property. The legacy `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` properties take `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so the mixin outputs invalid declarations for those values. It only works today for `center` and `baseline`.

findings.title: Panel positioned with order/auto margin while the other flex children rely on defaults
findings.detail: The header `.contents` becomes a flex container and `.panel` gets `order: 3` and `margin-left: auto`. Other children, such as the logo and any clearfix pseudo-elements on `.contents`, become flex items with default order 0 and are no longer laid out as floats. The `.valign-helper` rule (height 100%, inline-block) is now meaningless in this layout.

findings.title: Substring origin check on postMessage allows spoofed origins
findings.detail: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so an origin like `http://d` or `https://` is accepted. Any window can send resize messages, and the check should be an exact origin comparison.

findings.title: open() on a user-influenced URL (SSRF / command execution via open-uri)
findings.detail: Kernel#open with a string derived from the embed_url request parameter can fetch internal hosts. In general `open` with a leading pipe executes commands. The embed_url host check is weak, since only the host is compared and not the scheme.

findings.title: Unescaped referer injected into inline JavaScript string
findings.detail: `request.referer` is attacker-controlled and placed in a JS string literal. ERB HTML-escaping does not prevent breaking out of the quote (e.g. via a backslash or newline), and there is no JS escaping. The postMessage target origin should be the validated embeddable host instead.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options set to nonstandard ALLOWALL
findings.detail: ALLOWALL is not a valid value. Browsers ignore it, which effectively removes framing protection for this page. The referer check also does not stop other sites from framing it, since the Referer header is spoofable and optional.

findings.title: Stale @topic_view when render 'loading' path, and malformed end-if
findings.detail: `<%- end if %>` is invalid ERB/Ruby syntax (a stray `if` modifier) and will raise at render time. The template also assumes @topic_view is non-nil, but TopicView.new may raise if the topic was deleted.

findings.title: Feed item handling can crash or mutate frozen strings / nil
findings.detail: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError if the item has no content (Atom with only description) and `scrub` needs Ruby 2.1+. In addition, `i.id` can be nil, so `TopicEmbed.import` is called with a nil URL and fails on the `=~` match. One bad item aborts the whole feed.

findings.title: import mutates caller's string and hashes content with appended footer
findings.detail: `contents <<` mutates the argument in place, which breaks with frozen strings and alters the caller's data. The SHA1 is computed on unabsolutized content, so it is consistent only by luck. Any raw-HTML content from remote feeds is stored as cooked unsanitized.

findings.title: Raw HTML posts are stored as cooked without sanitization
findings.detail: For raw_html posts `cook` returns the raw remote HTML verbatim. It is rendered with `raw post.cooked` on the forum and in the embed, so feed or page content with scripts yields stored XSS.

findings.title: Default cook_method of 1 maps to regular only if Enum is 1-based
findings.detail: The default of 1 is hardcoded to match Enum's first value; this is brittle but acceptable. More critically, the migration file for MigrateWordCounts and others were modified (force: true on create_table in an existing migration), which can drop existing top_topics data when re-run.

findings.title: Test expects TopicRetriever to be invoked but controller enqueues a job
findings.detail: The controller calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic) rather than TopicRetriever.new directly. Jobs run inline only in some configurations, and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` may never fire if queue_jobs is false in test, while the mocha expectation is verified only loosely.

findings.title: Port comparison omits scheme and mutates frozen/interpolated prefix
findings.detail: Non-default port logic excludes only 80 and 443 regardless of scheme, so http on 443 loses its port. The prefix drops the port for the wrong scheme pairing.

findings.title: Substring origin check on postMessage allows spoofed origins
findings.detail: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl, including an empty or "null" prefix, passes. Other origins can then control the iframe height, and the check is not a real origin comparison.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options set to non-standard ALLOWALL
findings.detail: ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options value; browsers ignore it, which leaves the header effectively unset and permits framing from any site. The embed should be restricted to the embeddable host, e.g. via CSP frame-ancestors.

findings.title: Referer-only host validation is spoofable and cached responses bypass it
findings.detail: Access control relies only on the Referer header, which non-browser clients can forge. A missing Referer raises InvalidAccess, so privacy-stripped requests fail. The embed also feeds an unauthenticated enqueue of retrieval jobs.
findings.evidence: raise Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('invalid referer host') if URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host

findings.title: Referer interpolated into inline JavaScript string
findings.detail: The request.referer value is HTML-escaped by ERB but not JavaScript-escaped inside a script block. A crafted Referer with a quote or a path containing special characters can break the string or cause an error. It should be built from the validated embeddable host with escape_javascript or to_json.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a URL string
findings.detail: open(url) from open-uri is used with a user-influenced embed_url (and a feed URL in PollFeed). If the string is not a plain http(s) URL, Kernel#open can access local files or run commands via a leading pipe. Also no timeouts or internal address restrictions.

findings.title: Imported HTML stored and served raw without sanitization; URL injected into markup
findings.detail: Posts with cook_method raw_html return raw untouched, so imported feed content (including script tags) is rendered as-is on the forum and in the embed. The url is also interpolated into an href attribute unescaped.

findings.title: Loading view rendered but expires header still applied; topic view never rendered with nil topic
findings.detail: When no topic exists, the loading page is cached for a minute via discourse_expires_in, so a reload every 30s may serve a stale loading page. Also best.html.erb dereferences @topic_view.topic.url and posts.present? only after the topic exists.

findings.title: Feed item fields may be nil causing crash and aborting the whole import
findings.detail: i.content may be nil for RSS items using description only, so i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the rest of the feed. String#scrub is also unavailable on older Rubies, and `url` may be nil if id is missing.

findings.title: import mutates the passed-in contents string
findings.detail: `contents <<` modifies the caller's string in place; the spec reuses a `let` string and frozen literals would raise. The hash is computed after the footer is appended, but repeated calls with the same string append the footer repeatedly.

findings.title: Malformed ERB conditional terminator
findings.detail: `<%- end if %>` is invalid syntax (end followed by a stray `if`) and will cause a template compile error.

findings.title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever.new but controller enqueues a job
findings.detail: The controller calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...), so the test stubs TopicRetriever.new and expects retrieve to be called, which only holds if jobs run inline. The test also asserts retrieve on a mock, and does not verify the loading branch.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx/expire throttle
findings.detail: If the process dies between setnx and expire, the key never expires and the URL is permanently throttled. Use a single SET with NX and EX or setex.

findings.title: Substring check on postMessage origin
findings.detail: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so an origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. `http://d`, or an empty/"null" style origin) passes. Messages from untrusted frames can therefore control iframe height.

findings.title: Unescaped referer injected into inline JavaScript
findings.detail: `request.referer` is client-controlled and is placed inside a JS string without JS escaping. ERB's HTML escaping does not stop quote or script-context breakouts, so a crafted Referer can allow script injection. It is also used as the postMessage targetOrigin, though the full URL is not an origin.

findings.title: Remote HTML stored and served raw without sanitization
findings.detail: Content from RSS or remote pages is saved with cook_method raw_html, which bypasses the cooking and sanitizing pipeline, and is output with `raw post.cooked`. Feed content containing scripts or event handlers will execute on the Discourse origin. The url is also interpolated unescaped into an href with single quotes.

findings.title: Kernel#open on URL allows SSRF and local file/command access
findings.detail: `open(url)` with open-uri follows redirects and fetches arbitrary hosts, including internal ones. The URL derives from the user-supplied embed_url, and only its host is compared to a setting. The same pattern in PollFeed uses `open` on a setting.

findings.title: Referer-only host check is spoofable and framing is open to all
findings.detail: Access control depends on the client-supplied Referer header. X-Frame-Options is set to ALLOWALL, so any site can frame it. The `embed_url` host is not checked against the referer in the controller.
findings.evidence: raise Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('invalid referer host') if URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host

findings.title: @topic_view nil in loading case; broken ERB conditional
findings.detail: When the topic is not found, 'loading' is rendered, but the controller continues. The `<%- end if %>` is invalid syntax. When the topic has no posts, `@topic_view.topic.url` is also not a valid absolute link.

findings.title: Feed item nil handling and abort on single bad item
findings.detail: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content (common in RSS with only description). `i.id` may also be nil, which makes import fail. One bad item aborts processing of the entire feed.

findings.title: Mutates caller's string and hashes content after appending footer
findings.detail: `contents <<` mutates the argument, which is possibly a frozen or shared string. The SHA is computed over the content with the footer, so absolutizing differs from the stored hash. In the spec, the same `let` string is mutated.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx/expire can leave a permanent throttle key
findings.detail: If the process dies between setnx and expire, the key never expires and the URL is blocked forever.

findings.title: Test expects TopicRetriever to be used but controller enqueues a job
findings.detail: The controller calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic) and never calls TopicRetriever directly. The expectation on TopicRetriever.new/retrieve cannot be satisfied unless the job runs inline, so the test is unreliable.

findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.detail: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields an extra empty page (e.g. 50 users with limit 50 gives 2 pages). The "next" button is therefore enabled on the real last page, and it advances to an offset equal to user_count, which shows an empty list.

findings.title: usernames input is never reset and stale usernames are re-submitted
findings.detail: After addMembers the usernames value is left in place (the code has a TODO acknowledging this), so the next click, or any retry, re-sends the same usernames. The user-selector box also keeps showing the names that were already added.

findings.title: remove_member passes an integer id to has_many delete
findings.detail: `group.users.delete(user_id)` is given an Integer rather than a User record. In Rails 4 this raises AssociationTypeMismatch (use delete_all/where or find the user first). The removal then fails with a 500 error, so the 'is able to remove a member' spec cannot pass.

findings.title: Nested member routes do not provide the :group_id param the controller expects
findings.detail: `delete "members"` and `put "members"` are declared inside `resources :groups` without a member block. Rails therefore nests them under `:group_id` and maps them to "groups#remove_member", which resolves to a controller under the admin namespace. The JS calls `/admin/groups/:id/members`, which does match, but the controller uses `params.require(:group_id)`, so these routes are fragile and easy to misconfigure.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined for an empty name, yet callers chain .then
findings.detail: The early return yields undefined instead of a promise. Any caller that chains on the result (e.g. controller actions that `return group.findMembers()`) will break, whereas the previous code returned a resolved promise.

findings.title: Member list ajax failures are unhandled and the list is never refreshed on errors
findings.detail: removeMember and addMembers have no error handler, so a 422 or 500 response is swallowed silently and the user gets no feedback. The chained findMembers() result is not returned either, so callers cannot wait for the reload.

findings.title: No bounds on limit and offset params
findings.detail: A client can send limit=0, a negative number or an enormous value, so the members endpoint can return the entire member list unpaginated or fail on a negative limit. The previous code applied a cap and these new params have no maximum.

findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.detail: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields an extra empty page when user_count is a multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users gives 2 pages). The next button is then enabled on the last real page and leads to an empty page.

findings.title: showingLast never true when currentPage is 0 / showingFirst mismatch with pagination state
findings.detail: The next action clamps offset to user_count, so with an exact multiple of limit the offset lands at user_count, which gives an empty page. currentPage is also only recomputed from limit/offset/user_count, which are set non-atomically.

findings.title: remove_member passes an id to has_many delete
findings.detail: group.users.delete(user_id) is given an Integer rather than a User record. In Rails 4 this raises AssociationTypeMismatch, so removal fails. The call should use a User object or delete_all with a condition.

findings.title: Nested member routes do not map to params and controller used by the code
findings.detail: The routes nested in resources :groups produce /admin/groups/:group_id/members, but they target "groups#remove_member" within the admin namespace. Because the action path form and the params differ, the routing may not resolve correctly. The spec also issues xhr :put, :remove_member, which the DELETE-only route does not accept.

findings.title: Test uses wrong HTTP verb for remove_member
findings.detail: The test sends PUT to remove_member, which is routed only for DELETE. The 422 path for automatic groups may never be exercised through the real route.

findings.title: Unbounded user-controlled limit and negative offset
findings.detail: limit and offset are taken directly from params with no upper bound or non-negative check. A client can request huge pages, and a negative limit or offset raises a DB error. The old code had at least a default cap.

findings.title: update/create changes behavior for missing visible and name; params[:name] set even if blank
findings.detail: update sets group.visible = (params[:visible] == "true") unconditionally, so a request lacking visible makes the group invisible. The new create also drops the usernames handling and uses default alias_level.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined in one branch and a promise in another
findings.detail: Callers like the controller's next/previous return group.findMembers() and may chain on it. Returning undefined for an empty name breaks such chaining. The new group form is also never loaded for new groups.

findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.detail: Math.floor(count/limit)+1 gives an extra empty page when count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users, limit 50 -> 2 pages). The 'next' button then stays enabled and pages to an empty list; use Math.ceil.

findings.title: remove_member passes a user id to the users association delete
findings.detail: group.users.delete(user_id) expects a record (or ids only via delete with ids on has_many through in specific forms); passing an Integer on a has_many :through can raise AssociationTypeMismatch or silently not remove the membership. Look up the User and delete the record, or use group_users.

findings.title: add_members/remove_member don't handle a missing group
findings.detail: The group is found with Group.find after `.to_i`, and the routes use nested `group_id`, but `delete "members"`/`put "members"` inside `resources :groups` generate `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`, which is fine; however usernames are split without stripping whitespace so entries like 'a, b' silently fail to match and are skipped with no feedback.

findings.title: Controller never refreshes members after changing group
findings.detail: Members are in `members` set on the model by findMembers, but when navigating between groups state like `usernames` input is retained and the model's offset persists across navigation, so a reopened group starts on a stale page. Also no input is cleared after adding, as the TODO admits.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined when name is empty
findings.detail: The early return yields undefined instead of a promise, while other paths return a promise; callers like the controller's next/previous return this value and may chain on it. Also add/remove member and its reload have no error handling.

findings.title: Unbounded limit parameter on members endpoint
findings.detail: The limit comes straight from the request with no upper cap, so a client can request all members of a large group (previously the limit applied only to automatic groups, now a negative/huge value is also passed through).

findings.title: ensure_loaded! skips LOAD_MUTEX and races with load_locale
findings.detail: ensure_loaded! lazily initializes @loaded_locales and checks include? outside the mutex. Concurrent requests can race on `||=` and the check, and `reload!` can swap the array underneath it. Because `load_locale` is the only synchronized path, this leaves a window for unsafe shared-state access.

findings.title: Locale type mismatch makes the loaded check ineffective
findings.detail: Fallback locales are symbols, but @loaded_locales may hold the strings or symbols that callers pass. `I18n.locale=` in set_locale can be given a String from SiteSetting.default_locale. If types differ, include? never matches and the locale is reloaded repeatedly.

findings.title: Fallback list does not handle a nil default_locale and runs at initialization time
findings.detail: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises NoMethodError if the setting is nil. The fallback hash is also consulted for every translation lookup, so the DB-backed SiteSetting is hit during early boot (before the DB or settings are ready) and on every lookup. In addition, the key passed may be a String, so the `uniq` call does not deduplicate a String locale against a Symbol one.

findings.title: Fallbacks module included into backend class at init, backend may be wrapped or not Simple
findings.detail: `I18n.backend.class` is evaluated at initializer time. If the backend is a lazily built object or a different class (e.g. a Chain), the module is included into the wrong class. Including Fallbacks also does not pass through the lazy-loading `load_translations` patch, so fallback locales are not loaded unless ensure_loaded! is called on every path (e.g. mailers, jobs).

findings.title: Fallback locales only loaded in controllers
findings.detail: ensure_loaded! is called only in the controller's set_locale. Background jobs, mailers and other code that set I18n.locale (e.g. with_locale) will have fallbacks enabled but fallback locales unloaded, producing missing translations. This path also runs an extra SiteSetting lookup on every request.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but only overrides []
findings.detail: Fallbacks code and `I18n.fallbacks=` expect hash-like behaviour (e.g. `fallbacks[locale]` and `map`). Only `[]` is overridden, so `fetch`, `key?` and similar methods behave inconsistently with it. Also, the class is defined as a top-level constant in an initializer.

findings.title: Fallbacks mixed into whatever backend class exists at initializer time
findings.detail: `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, ...)` includes Fallbacks into the class of the current backend instance, which is not guaranteed to be Simple, and it runs eagerly. It also loads before/after the freedom patch, so the translate_accelerator `load_translations` override and `available_locales` may not interact as intended. Including Fallbacks after Pluralization also changes the lookup chain order.

findings.title: SiteSetting accessed in fallback lookup; may fail or hit DB on every lookup
findings.detail: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` is invoked on every missing-translation lookup and reads `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`. During early boot, rake tasks, or migrations the DB/SiteSetting may be unavailable. If default_locale is nil it raises NoMethodError.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! races on @loaded_locales and locale type mismatch
findings.detail: The unsynchronized `@loaded_locales ||= []` and `include?` check happen outside LOAD_MUTEX. Also `load_locale` loads rb files only when `@loaded_locales.empty?`, so ensuring the fallback locale first (before the main one) is fine, but a locale passed as a string vs symbol is stored differently and may be loaded twice. `reload!` resets the array to empty, so concurrent requests can see inconsistent state.

findings.title: Fallback locale loading on every request in set_locale
findings.detail: `ensure_loaded!` runs on every request, which calls SiteSetting.default_locale and builds arrays each time. It's also called for the non-translating fast path, adding overhead to every controller action.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! does not load fallbacks for non-request code and translate cache ignores fallbacks
findings.detail: `ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from the controller, so mailers, jobs, and `I18n.with_locale` blocks won't load the fallback locales, leaving fallbacks silently missing. Also the `translate` LRU cache key uses only the locale, so cached results from before the fallback was loaded remain.

findings.title: Fallbacks hash subclass not a real Hash for I18n::Locale::Fallbacks API
findings.detail: `I18n.fallbacks` is expected to be an `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` instance (supports `map`, `defaults`). Replacing it with a Hash subclass overriding only `[]` breaks other callers (e.g. `fetch`, `defaults=`), and the removal of `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from the environment files changes behavior for development/test too.

findings.title: Fallback chain computed from locale type mismatch (string vs symbol)
findings.detail: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq` only dedupes if `locale` is a symbol. `set_locale` assigns `SiteSetting.default_locale`, a String, to I18n.locale, which is converted to a symbol, but callers of `fallbacks[]` may pass strings. The mixed types produce duplicate entries and inconsistent `ensure_loaded!` keys.

findings.title: Fallback lookup depends on SiteSetting/DB at arbitrary times
findings.detail: The fallbacks hash calls SiteSetting.default_locale on every lookup, including during boot, rake tasks, or before the DB/settings are available. This can raise or hit the DB on each translation fallback lookup, and `.compact` runs after `.to_sym` so it cannot guard a nil default_locale (nil.to_sym raises).

findings.title: Unsynchronized check-then-load and lazy init of @loaded_locales
findings.detail: `ensure_loaded!` lazily initializes `@loaded_locales` and checks inclusion outside LOAD_MUTEX. `load_locale` rechecks inside the lock, but the `||=` initialization is racy and can replace an array another thread is appending to, losing loaded-state. The `@loaded_locales.empty?` branch in `load_locale` also depends on this.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! on every request computes fallbacks via SiteSetting
findings.detail: Calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in a before filter on every request re-evaluates the fallback list and performs loaded checks each time. It is needed only when the locale changes.

findings.title: Fallbacks module included into I18n.backend.class at initializer time
findings.detail: `I18n.backend.class` is evaluated at load time and may be a wrapper or different class than Simple, depending on initialization order. It relies on a comment-only ordering ('after 02-freedom_patches.rb'). Fallbacks is also not applied to the Simple class that the pluralization is added to.

findings.title: Negative slicing on Django QuerySet raises AssertionError
findings.detail: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a negative cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise an AssertionError, so the comment claiming the ORM handles it is wrong and the request returns a 500.

findings.title: Negative offsets claimed to expose data beyond pagination bounds
findings.detail: The code comment says negative offsets give access to data beyond normal pagination bounds and that this is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level. A user-controlled cursor offset is used unvalidated, and the stop arithmetic with a negative start can produce wrong or oversized slices.
findings.evidence: start_offset = cursor.offset  # Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination

findings.title: Existing BasePaginator now permits negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.detail: The shared BasePaginator was changed so that when cursor.is_prev is true the raw offset is used with no clamping. A client-supplied negative offset in a prev cursor reaches queryset slicing for every paginator, causing an AssertionError (500). The comment says negative offsets are allowed, but the code only clamps for non-prev cursors.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: Prev-cursor trimming uses unclamped offset inconsistent with slice start
findings.detail: The trim check compares len(results) to offset + limit + extra, while the query used start_offset. In the non-advanced path or after clamping, these can differ, so the extra row is not dropped and pages are wrong. The same discrepancy applies to the original paginator.

findings.title: Possible crash when member is None for superuser access
findings.detail: organization_context.member can be None (e.g. superuser not in the org), so accessing .member.has_global_access raises AttributeError. The `or` only short-circuits when the user is a superuser. A non-superuser without membership is already blocked, but the expression is fragile and evaluated on every request, even without the optimized flag.

findings.title: Undocumented query flag toggles a different paginator
findings.detail: An optional user-controlled query param switches the audit log endpoint to an experimental paginator that has behavior differing from the default. This adds an untested code path whose only difference is the unsafe negative-offset support.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are allowed but nothing changes
findings.detail: The added comment says Cursor allows negative offsets for efficient reverse pagination, but the code simply does int(offset). It documents behavior that is misleading and hides that negative offsets are unvalidated.
findings.evidence: # Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios

findings.title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet raises or crashes
findings.detail: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a negative cursor.offset into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError, so a crafted cursor with a negative offset gives a 500. The comment that the ORM handles negative slicing is wrong.
findings.evidence: start_offset = cursor.offset  # Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination

findings.title: Feature gate relies on member attribute that may be missing
findings.detail: organization_context.member can be None, for example for a superuser who is not a member of the org. Evaluating `.has_global_access` then raises AttributeError. The `or` short-circuits only when the user is a superuser, so non-superusers without membership crash. This also ties an unusual pagination mode to a loosely defined privilege check.

findings.title: Existing BasePaginator behavior changed; comment contradicts code
findings.detail: The comment says negative offsets are allowed, but the code clamps non-prev offsets to 0 and still passes negative offsets for prev cursors. A negative offset on a prev cursor reaches the queryset slice and crashes. Clamping also changes pagination behavior for every paginator that inherits this method. The later check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` still uses the unclamped offset, so it is inconsistent with the slice.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: Prev-cursor trimming uses the unclamped offset
findings.detail: The trimming check compares the result length against `offset + limit + extra`, but the query actually used `start_offset`. When the two differ (for example a clamped offset or a negative offset), the extra row is never dropped, or the wrong row is dropped.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates the BasePaginator logic and mixes up key handling
findings.detail: The class copies the whole get_result and uses Paginator-style get_item_key, which applies math.floor to a datetime. The audit log key is `datetime`, so math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError once results are built. DateTimePaginator's conversion is needed here.
findings.evidence: return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))

findings.title: value_from_cursor returns a raw value that is incompatible with datetime filtering
findings.detail: For the datetime ordering used by the audit log, the cursor value is a millisecond timestamp. Returning it unchanged, instead of converting to a datetime as DateTimePaginator does, makes the extra WHERE clause compare a datetime column to a raw number. This breaks or wrongly filters results when a cursor is supplied.

findings.title: Negative slice on Django QuerySet raises instead of paginating
findings.detail: The advanced path slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`), but Django QuerySets raise an AssertionError for negative indexing. The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is wrong, so a crafted cursor with a negative offset yields a server error (500).

findings.title: Negative offsets bypass pagination bounds, with a false safety claim
findings.detail: The code allows user-supplied negative offsets via the cursor and claims it exposes data 'beyond normal pagination bounds', asserting permissions are checked at the queryset level. Offsets are attacker-controlled through the cursor query parameter, and the justification does not guard against the resulting unbounded or odd slicing.
findings.evidence: # This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level

findings.title: Prev cursors still pass negative offsets to slicing in base paginator
findings.detail: The modified BasePaginator code only clamps the offset when not is_prev. A prev cursor with a negative offset (parsed from user input via Cursor.from_string) is passed straight into queryset slicing, causing an AssertionError. The comment says negative offsets are 'safe' but the behavior is a crash; it also changes behavior for all paginators in the codebase.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: Prev-page trimming uses unadjusted offset in new paginator
findings.detail: The trimming check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the raw `offset`, not the `start_offset` that was actually sliced. With negative or clamped offsets the computed length never matches, so the extra row is not dropped and pages get an extra item.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError on member and unclear privilege gating
findings.detail: `organization_context.member` can be None (e.g. for superusers who are not members), and the `or` evaluates `.member.has_global_access` whenever the user is not a superuser, so non-member access may crash. The gating also lets any global-access member enable a risky paginator through a query param.

findings.title: Duplicated paginator logic copy-pasted from BasePaginator
findings.detail: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result wholesale, and its else branch is identical to the already-modified base. Behavior differs only in the unsafe negative-offset path, so the duplication adds risk of drift without benefit.

findings.title: Privileged paginator path unlocks negative-offset access to audit log rows
findings.detail: Any org member with global access can send `optimized_pagination=true` and a cursor with a negative offset. This reaches `OptimizedCursorPaginator` negative slicing, which Django querysets reject with an AssertionError (a 500). The 'beyond normal pagination bounds' comment is also false, since the queryset is already filtered by organization.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing is unsupported by Django ORM
findings.detail: The code assumes the ORM handles negative slicing, but Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. A user-supplied negative cursor offset therefore crashes the request. A stop computed as negative offset plus limit is also meaningless.

findings.title: Behavior change in shared BasePaginator clamps negative offsets for all paginators
findings.detail: The base `get_result` now clamps non-prev offsets to 0 but passes negative offsets through for prev cursors, which still crashes in Django. The comment says 'allow negative offsets' while the code clamps, which contradicts it. The later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check also uses the unclamped offset.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: span_count only reflects the last merge, and ZUNIONSTORE ignores the trimming order
findings.detail: `span_count` is overwritten by each ZUNIONSTORE, so it reflects the final union size only when a merge happened.
